verses.text: Then the king sent for all the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, and they came together to meet him.

The king went up to the LORD's temple with all the people of Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem, along with the priests and the prophets. All the people came, from the least important to the most important. He read aloud to them all the words of the Book of the Covenant, which had been found in the LORD's temple.

The king stood by the pillar and made a covenant in the LORD's presence. He promised to follow the LORD and keep his commands, his teachings, and his laws with all his heart and all his soul. He promised to carry out the words of the covenant written in this book. And all the people promised to keep the covenant.

The king ordered Hilkiah the high priest, the priests next in rank, and the doorkeepers to take out of the LORD's temple all the objects made for Baal, for Asherah, and for all the stars in the sky. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron Valley and carried the ashes to Bethel.

He got rid of the pagan priests the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense at the high places in the towns of Judah and around Jerusalem. He also got rid of those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, the moon, the planets, and all the stars in the sky.
He took the Asherah pole out of the LORD's temple to the Kidron Valley outside Jerusalem. He burned it there, ground it to powder, and scattered the dust over the graves of the common people.
He tore down the rooms of the male shrine prostitutes, which were in the LORD's temple, where women wove coverings for Asherah.

Josiah brought all the priests from the towns of Judah to Jerusalem. He made the high places where they had burned incense unfit for worship, from Geba to Beersheba. He tore down the shrines at the gates, at the entrance of the Gate of Joshua, the city governor, which was on the left as you go through the city gate.
The priests of the high places were not allowed to serve at the LORD's altar in Jerusalem, but they ate bread made without yeast with their fellow priests.
He made Topheth, in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, unfit for worship, so no one could sacrifice a son or daughter in the fire to Molech there.

He removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun. They had been kept at the entrance to the LORD's temple, near the room of an official named Nathan-Melech, in the courtyard. Then Josiah burned the chariots dedicated to the sun.

The king tore down the altars the kings of Judah had built on the roof near the upstairs room of Ahaz. He also tore down the altars Manasseh had built in the two courtyards of the LORD's temple. He smashed them to pieces there and threw the rubble into the Kidron Valley.

The king also made unfit for worship the high places east of Jerusalem, on the south side of the Hill of Corruption. King Solomon of Israel had built them for Ashtoreth, the disgusting goddess of the Sidonians, for Chemosh, the disgusting god of Moab, and for Milcom, the disgusting god of the Ammonites.
Josiah smashed the sacred stone pillars and cut down the Asherah poles, and he covered the places where they had stood with human bones.
He also tore down the altar at Bethel and the high place made by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin. He burned the high place, ground it to powder, and burned the Asherah pole.

Then Josiah looked around and saw the tombs on the hillside. He had the bones taken out of the tombs and burned them on the altar to make it unfit for worship. This happened just as the LORD had said through the man of God who announced these things long before.

Josiah asked, "What is that grave marker I see?" The people of the town told him, "It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and announced the very things you have done to the altar at Bethel."
Josiah said, "Leave it alone. Do not let anyone move his bones." So they left his bones alone, along with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
Josiah also removed all the shrines on the high places in the towns of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had built and which had made the LORD angry. He did to them just what he had done at Bethel.
He killed all the priests of those high places on their own altars, and he burned human bones on the altars. Then he went back to Jerusalem.
The king gave this order to all the people: "Celebrate the Passover to the LORD your God, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant."
No Passover like this one had been celebrated since the days when the judges led Israel, not in all the time of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, this Passover was celebrated to the LORD in Jerusalem.

Josiah also got rid of the people who talked with spirits of the dead, the fortune-tellers, the household gods, the idols, and all the other disgusting things seen in Judah and Jerusalem. He did this to obey the words of the Law written in the book Hilkiah the priest had found in the LORD's temple.
There was never a king like Josiah, before him or after him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart, all his soul, and all his strength, obeying all the Law of Moses.
Even so, the LORD did not turn away from his great, burning anger against Judah, because of all the things Manasseh had done to make him angry.
The LORD said, "I will also remove Judah from my presence, as I removed Israel. I will reject Jerusalem, the city I chose, and the temple, the place where I said, 'My name will be there.'"
The rest of what Josiah did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
While Josiah was king, Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt went up to the Euphrates River to help the king of Assyria. King Josiah marched out to fight him, but when Necho met him at Megiddo, he killed him.

Josiah's officials carried his body in a chariot from Megiddo to Jerusalem and buried him in his own tomb. Then the people of the land took Josiah's son Jehoahaz, anointed him, and made him king in his father's place.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for three months. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, just as his ancestors had done.

Pharaoh Necho put him in chains at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so he could not rule in Jerusalem. He forced Judah to pay about three thousand four hundred kilograms of silver and about thirty-four kilograms of gold.
Pharaoh Necho made Josiah's son Eliakim king in place of his father Josiah, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz to Egypt, and Jehoahaz died there.
Jehoiakim paid Pharaoh the silver and gold he demanded. To do this, he taxed the land. He made each person pay silver and gold according to what they owned, to give to Pharaoh Necho.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother was Zebidah, the daughter of Pedaiah, from Rumah.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, just as his ancestors had done.
